info.name: mux REST API
info.description:
Postman collection for the optional local **mux** REST + WebSocket server (`mux serve`).

The server is opt-in, binds to loopback (`127.0.0.1`) by default, and — unless started with `--no-auth` — requires a local API key sent as a bearer token. It exposes mux's in-process services (endpoints, MCP servers, prompts, subagents, hooks, keybindings, skills, sessions, chat, settings) plus durable **usage telemetry** and **pricing**.

## Getting started
1. Start the server: `mux serve` (it prints the base URL and, on first run, an auto-generated API key). Or `mux serve --no-auth` for keyless local use.
2. Set the collection variables: **baseUrl** (default `http://127.0.0.1:8710`) and **apiKey** (the printed key; leave blank when using `--no-auth`).
3. Collection-level auth applies a bearer token from **apiKey** to every request except those in the **Health** folder, which is anonymous.

All paths are versioned under `/v1.0/api`. Full reference: `docs/REST_API.md`. Loopback uses `127.0.0.1` deliberately (on Windows `localhost` resolves IPv6 `::1` first and stalls).

variable.description: Scheme, host, and port the server listens on. Uses 127.0.0.1 (not localhost) to avoid Windows IPv6 first-resolution latency.
Local bearer API key printed by `mux serve`. Leave blank when the server runs with --no-auth.
An endpoint name used by the delete/chat examples.
A saved session id, used by the session export/delete examples.
A skill id, used by the skill detail/enable/delete examples.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness and version. The only anonymous surface — no API key required, so this folder overrides the collection bearer auth with `noauth`.

request.description: Returns `{ Status, Product, Version, Pid, StartedUtc, Uptime, TimestampUtc }`. `Status` is `healthy` while the server is up. Use this for readiness probes; it never requires auth.

item.name: Endpoints
item.description: The model endpoints in `endpoints.json` — the local and cloud LLMs mux can talk to. Secrets (API keys, header values) are never returned; a blank secret on write preserves the stored value. Edits are applied as a whole-collection PUT.

request.description: Lightweight list for pickers: `{ Items: [ { Name, AdapterType, BaseUrl, Model, IsDefault } ], Count }`. No secrets.
Full editable fields for each endpoint with secrets masked (`ApiKeySet` boolean instead of the key; header values blanked). Use this as the source for the PUT round-trip.

Replaces the whole endpoint collection. Send the full list (the dashboard edits client-side, then PUTs everything). A blank `apiKey` (or blank header value) preserves the stored secret; a non-blank value overwrites it. Returns the saved, masked list.
Deletes one endpoint by name. Returns the remaining masked list.

item.name: MCP Servers
item.description: MCP tool servers in `mcp-servers.json` that expose extra tools to the agent. Auth secrets are masked/preserved on the same blank-keeps-stored convention as endpoints.

request.description: Returns the configured MCP servers with any auth secret masked.
Replaces the whole MCP-server collection. Blank auth secret preserves the stored value.
Deletes one MCP server by name.

item.name: Prompts
item.description: System-prompt profiles in `prompts.json`. A blank system prompt inherits the built-in default.

request.description: Returns the prompt profiles (name, active flag, system prompt).
Replaces the prompt-profile collection.

item.name: Subagents
item.description: Subagent definitions in `subagents.json` the model can delegate scoped tasks to via the `spawn_subagent` tool.

request.description: Returns the subagent definitions.
Replaces the subagent collection.

item.name: Hooks & Commands
item.description: The plugin config in `hooks.json`: out-of-process event hooks and custom `/slash` commands. Saved together as one object.

request.description: Returns `{ hooks: [...], commands: [...] }`.
Replaces the plugin config.

item.name: Keybindings
item.description: Command-id → key-chord overrides in `keybindings.json`. A blank chord unbinds the command.

request.description: Returns the command-id → chord override map.
Replaces the keybinding overrides.

item.name: Skills
item.description: Skills under the skills directory — versioned Markdown-plus-code capabilities. List, inspect, toggle enablement, or delete.

request.description: Returns each skill's name, description, enabled/valid flags, and command count.
Returns one skill with its `SKILL.md` body.
Enables or disables a skill by id.
Deletes a skill folder by id.

item.name: Sessions
item.description: Persisted chat sessions under `~/.mux/sessions`. List, export to HTML/Markdown, or delete.

request.description: Returns saved sessions (id, title, endpoint, model, timestamps).
Renders a session to `{ format, filename, content }` for download.
Deletes a session by id.

item.name: Chat
item.description: A plain, tool-free chat completion against a configured endpoint — for the dashboard chat surface. It does not run the agent loop or expose tools.

request.description: Streams the completion server-side and returns the buffered result plus timing: `{ role, content, endpoint, model, stats: { ttftMs, streamingMs, totalMs, inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens } }`. This call is also recorded to usage telemetry (call kind `chat`).

item.name: Settings
item.description: The editable settings subset over `settings.json`. Secrets are masked (for example `rest.apiKeySet` instead of the key); the REST API key changes only when a non-blank `rest.apiKey` is supplied.

request.description: Returns the current settings with secrets masked.
Updates settings (validated/clamped, written to settings.json). Send only the fields you intend to change.

item.name: Usage Telemetry
item.description:
Read-only analytics over the shared usage database (`~/.mux/usage.db`), written by every mux instance on the machine. Every query accepts a time window as explicit `from`/`to` (Unix epoch **milliseconds**) or a `range` keyword (`hour`|`day`|`week`|`month`|`all`), plus optional `endpoint`, `model`, and `callKind` filters. When telemetry is disabled these endpoints return empty results (and `/filters` reports `Enabled: false`).

Every `Metrics` object carries: `Calls`, `Errors`, `ErrorRate`, `InputTokens`, `CachedTokens`, `OutputTokens`, `TotalTokens`, `CostUsd`, `CacheHitRate`, `AvgTtftMs`, `P50/P95/P99TtftMs`, `AvgTotalMs`, `P50/P95/P99TotalMs`, `AvgStreamMs`, `AvgTokensPerSec`.

request.description: Window KPI summary: `{ FromUnixMs, ToUnixMs, Metrics }`. Backs the dashboard KPI strip and the TUI /usage view.
Bucketed series for charting: `{ Items: [ { BucketStartUnixMs, Metrics } ], Count }`.
Totals grouped by a dimension, sorted by cost: `{ Items: [ { Dimension, Value, Metrics } ], Count }`.
Paginated raw per-call history (newest first) with derived `CostUsd` per row: `{ Items, TotalCount, PageNumber, PageSize }`.

query.description: The usage-event row id to delete (from an events row's Id).

request.description: Deletes one recorded call by its row id. Returns `{ Deleted: <count> }`.
Distinct endpoints and models seen in the store, for filter controls, plus `{ Enabled }` (false when telemetry is disabled).

item.name: Pricing
item.description: The user-editable model pricing table in `pricing.json` used to derive usage cost at read time. **Note:** unlike most mux DTOs, pricing serializes camelCase (`version`, `models`, `inputPerMTok`, `cachedInputPerMTok`, `outputPerMTok`).

request.description: Returns `{ version, models: { "<model>": { inputPerMTok, cachedInputPerMTok, outputPerMTok } } }` (curated defaults when the file is absent).
Replaces the whole pricing table. Rates are USD per million tokens. Returns the saved table. A rate change re-values historical cost immediately (cost is computed at read time).
